The eruption had been treated with topical medium potency 39 corticosteroids for several weeks without improvement. Physical examination revealed 40 multiple isolated and clustered scaly erythematous flat papules, 2 to 4 millimeters in 41 diameter, distributed on the left side of the trunk wall, over the left abdomen, flank and 42 upper back. The lesions were limited to these particular areas, and were arranged in a 43 linear, haphazardly blaschkoid distribution (Figure 1). Dermoscopy revealed shiny 44 whitish striae on the surface of some lesions. The eruption began a few days after 45 receiving the first dose of intramuscular COVID-19 vaccine (Pfizer/BioNTech 46 BNT162b2) in her left arm. The patient denied any reaction with the initial injection site or any changes to the eruption after the second dose of the vaccine she received 3 weeks 48 later. 49 A skin biopsy revealed a diffuse lichenoid lymphocytic infiltrate in the upper dermis and 50 around the hair follicles, with interface vacuolar changes, foci of spongiosis, and the lichenoid/lichen planus-like eruption. 53The patient was diagnosed with a lichenoid blaschkoid unilateral eruption (blaschkitis).54She was treated with a short course or oral corticosteroids and high potency topical 55 corticosteroids.
